theorem_title: A common index satisfying dimension-error and growth margins
natural_language_statement: Let θ, A, B, C, η, a, b, ε, and target be real numbers satisfying θ > 0, B > 0, C > 1, CB < 1, 1 < Cθ/B, 1 < B/A, η > 0, a ≥ 0, b ≥ 0, and ε > 0. Then there is a natural number m ≥ 1 such that (a m + b)/dimensionV(θ,B,C,m) + 100·dimensionK(C,m)/dimensionW(B,m) < ε, and target < η²(B/A)^m/(2(m+1)).
explanation: The dimension-error majorant tends to zero under the hypotheses C > 1, CB < 1, B > 0, and 1 < Cθ/B, so it is eventually below ε. Since B/A > 1 and η > 0, the quantity η²(B/A)^m/(2(m+1)) tends to infinity, so it is eventually above target. Also C^m eventually exceeds 2, providing the auxiliary lower bound required by the dimension-error estimate. Choose m beyond all these thresholds and at least 1; then both strict inequalities hold at the same index. The source is OpenAI math family 017 at commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a.
